$comment:
A2A decision->TaskState mapping corpus, v0.

WHAT THIS PINS.
One fixed vector per LEGAL (outcome, reason_code) pair, plus the fulfillment_owner
split for APPROVAL_REQUIRED, plus negative vectors for pairs the decision engine
cannot produce. Both SDKs must feed these through the SHIPPED mapping function
(see conformance/runners.v0.json) -- a runner that re-derives the table inline
proves nothing.

WHY THE LEGAL SET IS 7, NOT 30.
reason_code is DERIVED from the outcome by the decision engine
(aegis-boundary-core@324efd18, engine/aegis-decision/src/decision.rs:118-142
`ReasonCode::derive`). Only BLOCKED branches, and it branches on a substring scan
of the recorded reason text with the scope test running FIRST. So the reachable
pair set is exactly the 7 rows in `legal_pairs`. A corpus built from the 5x6
product would spend most of its vectors on states that cannot occur, and -- worse
-- would let a real missing pair hide among unreachable ones. `legal_pairs` is
declared here so completeness itself is testable.

SCOPE LIMIT.
This inventory holds for the check-boundary decision surface only. Other endpoints
emit reason codes outside this enum (e.g. `capsule_scope_denied` from the gateway's
backup-roots surface), which is why the validator is surface-scoped and
fail-closed on unknown values rather than an allowlist of everything seen on the
wire.

STATE OWNERSHIP.
`task_state_recommendation: null` means the mapping sets NO state. PROTECTED and
ACCESS_REDUCED do not make a task successful -- only the task executor knows
whether a withheld field was required for the requested result. The mapping never
selects a terminal state on the executor's behalf.

entries.why: Served within boundary. Nothing about the task lifecycle changed.
Narrowing is the product working. The mapping still does not declare the task successful.
The boundary runs the extra check. WORKING is the only state meaning 'still processing, you need do nothing'.
A2A spec 7.6.1: requesting that the CLIENT fulfil an authorization MUST transition to AUTH_REQUIRED.
A2A spec 7.6 frames AUTH_REQUIRED as DELEGATING fulfilment to the client. An approval the boundary resolves itself must not interrupt the client.
A policy refusal is a decision, not an error, and resubmitting will not repair it.
A scope that could not be resolved is a request defect the client can repair. REJECTED is terminal and would foreclose the repair.
Fail-secure refusal on internal error IS an error, and must stay distinguishable from a policy refusal.

negative_entries.why: The engine derives minimum_disclosure only for PROTECTED/ACCESS_REDUCED. A BLOCKED decision carrying it did not come from the check-boundary surface.
Contradictory: served within boundary AND refused by policy.
A review fix in the engine made CHECK_REQUIRED carry its own reason code, distinct from approval_required. Collapsing them again must be caught.
A real reason code from a DIFFERENT gateway surface. Fail-closed: the mapping is scoped to the check-boundary vocabulary and must not guess.
A future or skewed engine value must not be silently mapped to a state.
Absent reason code must fail closed, not default to policy_denied.

Without knowing who fulfils the approval the mapping cannot choose between AUTH_REQUIRED and WORKING. Guessing either way is a protocol error: guessing 'client' spuriously delegates and takes on 7.6.1 duties the boundary may not meet; guessing 'agent' silently drops a required client action.

Round-3 codex P1 cross-language divergence: a bare string spread to ['s','s','n'] in Node and shipped as field names, while Python rejected it. Both now reject a non-array withheld_fields as invalid_withheld_fields.
An empty field name is not a name; both languages reject it.
Round-3 codex P1: a null decision is a malformed input coerced to unknown_outcome, not a raw crash. Node threw a TypeError; both now raise A2AMappingError.
